---
title: "Workshop Datasets"
---

This page describes the datasets the workshop uses, where to download them, and where to put them so the tutorials can find them. Where possible, we use the **same datasets as Khushbu Patel's [YouTube Tutorials](https://github.com/kpatel427/YouTubeTutorials)** so that her video walkthroughs serve as supplementary material.

## Expected directory layout

By convention every tutorial reads from `../data/` --- i.e. a `data/` folder at the repository root. After you finish downloading, your tree should look like:

```
scrnaseq_workshop/
├── tutorials/
│   ├── Tutorial_01_QC_Preprocessing.qmd
│   └── ...
└── data/
    ├── filtered_feature_bc_matrix/                # scRNA (Tut 01-05)
    │   ├── barcodes.tsv.gz
    │   ├── features.tsv.gz
    │   └── matrix.mtx.gz
    ├── atac_v1_pbmc_10k_filtered_peak_bc_matrix.h5  # scATAC (Tut 06)
    ├── atac_v1_pbmc_10k_fragments.tsv.gz (+ .tbi)   # scATAC (Tut 06)
    ├── atac_v1_pbmc_10k_singlecell.csv              # scATAC (Tut 06)
    └── GSE152418_p20047_Study1_RawCounts.txt        # WGCNA (Tut 07)
```

If your layout differs, adjust the file paths inside each tutorial.

## Getting through 10x Genomics' click-through TOS

The 10x CDN at `cf.10xgenomics.com` serves dataset files **but returns HTTP 403** to a fresh `wget`/`curl` until you've accepted 10x's terms-of-use click-through at least once from a browser on the same network.

The first time you hit any 10x dataset, do this:

1.  Open the dataset's landing page in a normal web browser (links below).
2.  Scroll to the **Output and supplemental files** section. Click **Download** on any file you want.
3.  10x will pop up a *Sign in or share data with us* dialog — accept it. The download starts.
4.  You can cancel that download — the click-through has unlocked the CDN for your session. Now `wget`/`curl` against the same URL works from your terminal, including over SSH from a cluster login node (the gating is per network / IP, not per browser).

If you're operating from a fresh cluster account where no browser is available, the easiest workaround is to download once on your laptop, then `scp` or `rsync` the file to the cluster.

::: callout-tip
**Verification.** A working URL responds with `200 OK` and a content-length matching the file size. A blocked URL responds with `403` and a tiny body (\~21 bytes). Use `curl -sI <url>` to check.
:::

## Tutorials 01–05 — 20k NSCLC DTC (10x 3' v3.1 Multiplex)

**What it is.** Twenty-thousand dissociated tumor cells (DTCs) pooled from **seven non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) donors**, run on the 10x Chromium **3' v3.1** assay with **CellPlex multiplexing** (CMO hashing). Every cell carries a gene-expression profile *and* a sample-of-origin barcode --- so downstream you get both heterogeneity and donor-level structure to integrate.

This is the **same dataset Patel uses** in [`singleCell_standard_workflow.R`](https://github.com/kpatel427/YouTubeTutorials/blob/main/singleCell_standard_workflow.R) — but we use the smaller **filtered** matrix (\~250 MB) instead of the 1.5 GB raw matrix because Cell Ranger has already trimmed empty-droplet barcodes for you.

-   Landing page: [10x Genomics — 20k NSCLC DTC, 3' v3.1 Multiplex](https://www.10xgenomics.com/datasets/20-k-mixture-of-nsclc-dt-cs-from-7-donors-3-v-3-1-multiplex-3-1-standard-6-0-0) (do the click-through here first — see section above)
-   Used in: Tutorials 01–05

### Download — filtered matrix (default, \~250 MB)

With `wget`:

```bash
mkdir -p data && cd data

wget https://cf.10xgenomics.com/samples/cell-exp/6.0.0/20k_NSCLC_DTC_3p_nextgem_Multiplex/20k_NSCLC_DTC_3p_nextgem_Multiplex_count_filtered_feature_bc_matrix.tar.gz

tar -xzf 20k_NSCLC_DTC_3p_nextgem_Multiplex_count_filtered_feature_bc_matrix.tar.gz
ls filtered_feature_bc_matrix/
# barcodes.tsv.gz  features.tsv.gz  matrix.mtx.gz
```

With `curl`:

```bash
mkdir -p data && cd data

curl -L -O https://cf.10xgenomics.com/samples/cell-exp/6.0.0/20k_NSCLC_DTC_3p_nextgem_Multiplex/20k_NSCLC_DTC_3p_nextgem_Multiplex_count_filtered_feature_bc_matrix.tar.gz

tar -xzf 20k_NSCLC_DTC_3p_nextgem_Multiplex_count_filtered_feature_bc_matrix.tar.gz
```

::: callout-tip
**Optional — raw matrix (\~1.5 GB).** If you want to practice running EmptyDrops yourself, also pull the raw HDF5:

```bash
wget https://cf.10xgenomics.com/samples/cell-exp/6.0.0/20k_NSCLC_DTC_3p_nextgem_Multiplex/20k_NSCLC_DTC_3p_nextgem_Multiplex_count_raw_feature_bc_matrix.h5
```
:::

## Tutorial 04 Primer — `airway` (Bioconductor)

**What it is.** Bulk RNA-seq of four primary human airway smooth muscle cell lines, treated **untreated** vs. **dexamethasone**, two technical replicates each → eight samples (Himes et al. 2014, *PLoS ONE*). Standard reference dataset for teaching DESeq2; the same data Patel uses in [`runDESeq2.R`](https://github.com/kpatel427/YouTubeTutorials/blob/main/runDESeq2.R).

-   Bioconductor landing page: <https://bioconductor.org/packages/airway/>
-   No manual download — the package ships with the data:

```r
BiocManager::install("airway")
library(airway); data(airway)
```

## Tutorial 06 — PBMC 10k scATAC-seq v1 (10x, hg19)

Used for the scATAC-seq tutorial. **Same dataset as Patel's** [`scATACSeq_standard_workflow.R`](https://github.com/kpatel427/YouTubeTutorials/blob/main/scATACSeq_standard_workflow.R) and the [Signac PBMC vignette](https://stuartlab.org/signac/articles/pbmc_vignette).

-   Landing page: [10x Genomics — PBMC 10k scATAC-seq v1 (hg19)](https://www.10xgenomics.com/datasets/10-k-peripheral-blood-mononuclear-cells-pbm-cs-from-a-healthy-donor-1-standard-1-1-0) (do the [click-through](#getting-through-10x-genomics-click-through-tos) here first if you haven't already)

With `wget`:

```bash
cd data

wget https://cf.10xgenomics.com/samples/cell-atac/1.0.1/atac_v1_pbmc_10k/atac_v1_pbmc_10k_filtered_peak_bc_matrix.h5
wget https://cf.10xgenomics.com/samples/cell-atac/1.0.1/atac_v1_pbmc_10k/atac_v1_pbmc_10k_singlecell.csv
wget https://cf.10xgenomics.com/samples/cell-atac/1.0.1/atac_v1_pbmc_10k/atac_v1_pbmc_10k_fragments.tsv.gz
wget https://cf.10xgenomics.com/samples/cell-atac/1.0.1/atac_v1_pbmc_10k/atac_v1_pbmc_10k_fragments.tsv.gz.tbi
```

With `curl`:

```bash
cd data

curl -L -O https://cf.10xgenomics.com/samples/cell-atac/1.0.1/atac_v1_pbmc_10k/atac_v1_pbmc_10k_filtered_peak_bc_matrix.h5
curl -L -O https://cf.10xgenomics.com/samples/cell-atac/1.0.1/atac_v1_pbmc_10k/atac_v1_pbmc_10k_singlecell.csv
curl -L -O https://cf.10xgenomics.com/samples/cell-atac/1.0.1/atac_v1_pbmc_10k/atac_v1_pbmc_10k_fragments.tsv.gz
curl -L -O https://cf.10xgenomics.com/samples/cell-atac/1.0.1/atac_v1_pbmc_10k/atac_v1_pbmc_10k_fragments.tsv.gz.tbi
```

::: callout-warning
The earlier "Next GEM v1.1" re-release of this sample is mapped to **hg38** (filenames prefixed `atac_v1_pbmc_10k_nextgem_*`). The tutorial assumes the **v1 / hg19** release because it pairs with `EnsDb.Hsapiens.v75`.
:::

## Tutorial 07 — GSE152418 (COVID-19 PBMC bulk RNA-seq)

**What it is.** PBMC bulk RNA-seq from a published cross-sectional study of COVID-19 patients (Arunachalam et al. 2020, *Science*). Severity gradient from healthy to ICU. Same dataset as Patel's [`WGCNA.R`](https://github.com/kpatel427/YouTubeTutorials/blob/main/WGCNA.R).

-   GEO landing page: <https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE152418>

With `wget`:

```bash
cd data
wget https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE152nnn/GSE152418/suppl/GSE152418_p20047_Study1_RawCounts.txt.gz
gunzip GSE152418_p20047_Study1_RawCounts.txt.gz
```

With `curl`:

```bash
cd data
curl -L -O https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE152nnn/GSE152418/suppl/GSE152418_p20047_Study1_RawCounts.txt.gz
gunzip GSE152418_p20047_Study1_RawCounts.txt.gz
```

From R via `GEOquery`:

```r
library(GEOquery)
getGEOSuppFiles("GSE152418", baseDir = "data")
```

## Reference / annotation datasets (no manual download)

These are loaded automatically by the relevant R packages on first use --- you don't need to download them manually, but they do need an internet connection the first time.

| Reference | Loaded by | Used in |
|---|---|---|
| `HumanPrimaryCellAtlasData()` | `celldex` | Tutorial 05 (SingleR) |
| Azimuth `pbmcref` (or NSCLC ref) | `Azimuth` / `SeuratData` | Tutorial 05 |
| `EnsDb.Hsapiens.v75` | Bioconductor | Tutorial 06 (scATAC) |

## Disk-space budget

| Dataset | Compressed | Extracted |
|---|---|---|
| 20k NSCLC DTC (filtered, default) | \~250 MB | \~700 MB |
| 20k NSCLC DTC (raw `.h5`, optional) | \~1.5 GB | \~1.5 GB (single file) |
| `airway` | \~3 MB | (loaded in-package) |
| PBMC 10k scATAC-seq | \~2.5 GB | \~5 GB |
| GSE152418 raw counts | \~7 MB | \~80 MB |
| Reference data (cached) | --- | \~500 MB |

Plan for **\~3–4 GB total** if you stick to the filtered NSCLC matrix; **\~6–8 GB total** if you also pull the raw NSCLC `.h5`.

## "I still can't download from 10x"

If `curl` / `wget` returns HTTP 403 even after the click-through, the most common causes are:

-   You're on a different network than the one where you accepted the click-through (the gating is per IP / network).
-   You're trying to pull a file from the *wrong* dataset variant — there are two NSCLC datasets with similar names; make sure your URL slug contains `multiplex-3-1-standard-6-0-0` and not `with-intronic-reads`.
-   Your URL has a typo. Double-check by `curl -sI <url>`: a real file responds with `200` and a `content-length` matching GB-sized data; a typo'd URL responds with `403` and a 21-byte body.

If you're behind a restrictive network, all of the files above are also mirrored on the workshop's Talapas project directory `/projects/<PIRG>/scrnaseq_workshop/data/` once your account is set up --- copy from there with `scp` or work directly on the cluster.
